title: inventory
description: What one reference is made of (Implementation Decisions 9): its sections, numbered equations, figures with captions and image files, tables, algorithms, theorems, appendices, and references, each with a locator a reader can follow back to the source. Every field says where it came from: latex is the flattened e-print source, aux the numbers and pages one compile wrote, html the arXiv HTML rendering, and a converter names itself with its version. The coverage audit of the absorb reads this file, so an item missing here is an item no reader is ever asked about.

slug.description: the directory under research/refs/ that holds this reference

source_type.description: what the inventory was built from: the e-print source, the arXiv HTML rendering, or a PDF

version.description: the version arXiv served, from the Content-Disposition filename

etag.description: the ETag the fetch carried; the cache key that never expires

from_cache.description: true when arXiv answered 304 and the local source was reused

main.description: the top-level .tex file, from 00README or the \documentclass grep

flattened_by.description: latexpand when it is installed, wayline when the in-house expander stood in

compiled.description: whether one pdflatex run produced the .aux the exact numbers come from

sha256.description: a PDF's digest, which is how a second pass knows the file is the one inventoried

converter.description: the structural converter that filled the items of a PDF (docling-2.126.0), or none when no converter ran or every one failed

references_by.description: what filled references and metadata of a PDF: grobid with its version, or none

formula_enrichment.description: whether the converter read formulas off the page as LaTeX, which is always OCR-derived

provenance.description: per field, what filled it; a field nothing could fill says none and waits for the reader pass

counts.description: what the inventory found, for the count-against-a-by-eye-count the milestone asks for

environments.description: every LaTeX environment inventoried, starred variants kept apart (align and align* are not the same question)

path.description: the flattened source or the extracted text, relative to refs/<slug>/

boxes.description: a PDF's word and character boxes and ruled tables, too many to hold here, in a file beside the inventory

key.description: the \bibitem key, or the converter's identifier

raw_images.description: every image file the source carries, whatever the document does with it

path.description:
the file inside an e-print, or #page=

&image= for an image embedded in a PDF

notes.description: what the chain could not do and what a reader is therefore asked for; a missing tool says so here

provenance.description: latex, aux, html, pdftoppm, none, or a converter with its version (docling-2.0.1)

id.description: the id the absorb's obligation list and the coverage audit use

environment.description: the LaTeX environment or the theorem kind: equation, align*, figure*, lemma

number.description: the number the document gives the item; null when it has none

latex.description: the item's source in exact form, or a converter's OCR-derived LaTeX when ocr is true

file.description: the image file, relative to refs/<slug>/

graphics.description: the \includegraphics targets as they resolved inside the source

locator.description: where a reader looks: <file>:<line> in the source, or a page and bbox in a PDF

ocr.description: true when the latex was read off an image rather than off the source, so it is never exact form

confirm.description: true when a reader has to confirm the field: an environment boundary, an unlabeled number

confirm_fields.description: which parts a reader has to confirm when confirm is true: number, latex, boundary (where an algorithm or theorem ends), meaning (what a figure shows), caption, cells

cells.description: a table's rows of cell text as the converter or the ruled-table finder read them
